answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to a scarce, time-locked bond whose issuance follows a dune-shaped decay curve, so mass registration becomes prohibitively costly. A zephyr-like randomized audit samples a thin thread of transaction graphs each epoch, cross-checking stake provenance across multi-unit auction rounds to flag collusive clusters. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
